pick.headline: Erich Honecker forced out; Egon Krenz takes over
pick.summary: On October 18, 1989, Erich Honecker was removed as leader of East Germany and replaced by Egon Krenz, the Politburo member responsible for security.
pick.significance: Honecker's fall showed the East German regime cracking under mass flight and protest; Krenz lasted barely seven weeks.
pick.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of October 18, 1989, carried East Berlin ADN on the SED Central Committee electing Egon Krenz general secretary after granting Honecker's request to go "for health reasons".
